quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a way to stay in control of a motorcycle during a turn?

options.text: Speed up through the turn.
Slow down before you turn.
Lean into the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up through the turn.
questions.explanation: To control your motorcycle in a turn, slow down before you enter it. Look where you want to go. Lean the motorcycle by pressing the handlebar. Gently increase throttle through the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: If a motorcyclist cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, they should:

options.text: Speed up before hitting the object.
Stay seated so the seat cushions the impact.
Hit the obstacle at about a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hit the obstacle at about a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle and must ride over it, slow down first. Approach it at about a 90-degree angle if you can.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of a motorcycle crash with other traffic?

options.text: On the highway.
At intersections.
On rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections have the highest risk of crashes between motorcycles and other vehicles. Be very careful when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: When you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, who has the right of way?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
You should go through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or lights, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle gives you the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake.
The rear brake.
The emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's stopping power. Use both front and rear brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous for a motorcyclist to ride next to another vehicle?

options.text: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
Other drivers can easily see you.
You cannot read road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous. The other vehicle could swerve into your lane and hit you. It could also block your way to escape if something dangerous happens.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on the back of slow-moving vehicles going less than 25 mph. Examples include construction equipment, farm machinery, and horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ____ or higher is considered intoxicated.

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Virginia, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means a person is intoxicated. Anyone who is intoxicated cannot legally drive a motor vehicle.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the edge of the road mean?

options.text: No parking is allowed.
The right edge of the traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the edge of the road shows where the traffic lane ends on the right side.

questions.question: If you have a passenger on your motorcycle, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride slower than usual.
Leave more distance to stop than usual.
Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle with a passenger handles differently because of the extra weight. Ride slower and allow more stopping distance. A passenger should hold firmly onto the passenger handgrips or the operator's waist, hips, or midsection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic
Right lane ends
Merge

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols. This sign warns that traffic ahead will merge.

questions.question: When riding over grooved pavement in a work zone, what should you do?

options.text: Look down to watch for changes in the road.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Move to the edge of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up when riding through a work zone. Ride slowly over grooved pavement.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your motorcycle until the dog loses interest.
Ride slowly toward the dog, then quickly speed up as it gets close.
Swerve around the dog.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slowly toward the dog, then quickly speed up as it gets close.
questions.explanation: If a dog approaches, slow down and shift down gears as you get close to it. Quickly speed up and ride away from the dog.

questions.question: Using all three lane positions is:

options.text: Not good because you won't get used to any part of a lane.
Not good because it confuses other drivers.
Good if you are adjusting to changing road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Good if you are adjusting to changing road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet?

options.text: All riders
Riders who have held their license for less than two years
Riders under age 21
No one is required to wear a helmet

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders under age 21
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, all motorcycle riders and passengers under age 21 must wear helmets and eye protection. Helmets and eye protection are strongly recommended for all riders.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, how should the following distance change?

options.text: Increase
Decrease
Stay the same

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The trailer adds weight, so the motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the part of the lane that other drivers can see you in as early as possible.
Stop at the sign or signal and proceed normally.
Flash your lights and use your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of the lane that other drivers can see you in as early as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you as soon as possible.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders to see better.
Turn your shoulders, but not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Is eye protection required?

options.text: Required for all riders
Recommended but not required
Only required for new riders

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all riders
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear eye protection on a moving motorcycle. A full face shield gives the best protection.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, where should you ride?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
Wherever you are most comfortable.
In the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of the lane when passing parked cars. This helps you avoid doors opening, people stepping out, and cars pulling out. Be ready to move if conditions change.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake immediately, then re-apply it.
Release the front brake immediately and only use the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately, then re-apply it.
questions.explanation: Release the front brake right away and then re-apply it. This helps you regain control.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where should your feet be?

options.text: On the footrests for balance.
With your toes pointing downward.
Relaxed.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the footrests for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not point your toes downward, as they could get caught between the road and the footrests.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcycle rider should NOT:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them more visible.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: Choose a visible lane position and cover the clutch and brakes. Reduce your speed when approaching an intersection. Avoid sudden speed or position changes that might confuse other drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Signal ahead.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the tire locked to stop more quickly.
Release the front brake and only use the rear brake.
Release the front brake immediately and re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately and re-apply it.
questions.explanation: Release the front brake pressure right away. Then re-apply pressure gradually and with control.

questions.question: When turning, what should you do?

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders, to look through the turn.
Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders, to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, keep your eyes level with the horizon, and do not turn your shoulders. Turning your shoulders can cause you to steer off course.

questions.question: Which statement about brakes is true?

options.text: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.
Both brakes are equally powerful.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful and provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean in the direction of the curve.
Slow down in the turn.
Turn by using only the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the curve.
questions.explanation: Always lean in the direction of the turn. Slow down before entering the turn, not during it.

questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, when should you return to your original lane?

options.text: When you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
As soon as the truck is behind you.
When you feel you have enough space.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your original lane only when you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
